# EvidenceCheck

EvidenceCheck is an evidence-first vendor due-diligence and public-signal analysis service for procurement, third-party risk, security/compliance teams and AI agents.

## Core buyer problem
Repeated vendor first-pass research is slow: teams collect public signals, copy notes, compare basic controls and still need to identify missing evidence and supplier follow-up questions. EvidenceCheck turns that repetitive first pass into narrow, composable machine tasks.

## Primary paid capabilities
- POST /web-extract — extract clean public webpage text, metadata, headings and links; from $0.005 USDC
- POST /site-audit — inspect observable website security signals such as HTTPS, security headers, cookie flags, robots.txt and security.txt; $0.01 USDC
- POST /vendor-preflight — combine public vendor signals into evidence gaps, risk indicators and concrete supplier questions; $0.025 USDC
- POST /analyze — analyze supplied business-document text
- /review-purchase — fixed-scope human-led vendor review

## Machine interfaces
- https://evidencecheck-api.onrender.com/openapi.json
- https://evidencecheck-api.onrender.com/skill.md
- https://evidencecheck-api.onrender.com/basedagents.json
- https://evidencecheck-api.onrender.com/.well-known/agent-card.json
- https://evidencecheck-api.onrender.com/stats
- https://evidencecheck-site.onrender.com/

## Payment
Paid machine endpoints use x402 with USDC on Base mainnet (eip155:8453). Payment is per request; no subscription is required for API calls.

## Recommended agent flow
1. Discover service metadata and OpenAPI.
2. Choose the narrowest endpoint that satisfies the task.
3. Send the request and follow the x402 payment challenge when required.
4. Parse the JSON result.
5. Preserve limitations and evidence gaps in downstream reasoning.
6. Ask the vendor or a qualified reviewer to verify material findings.

## Trust boundary
Outputs are first-pass evidence and public signals. They are not certification, a penetration test, a legal opinion, proof of compliance, or proof that a vendor is secure. Material findings require appropriate human verification.

## Best-fit buyer
Procurement and third-party-risk workflows that repeatedly need to answer: what can we observe publicly, what evidence is missing, and what should we ask the supplier next?

## Commercial positioning
EvidenceCheck is intentionally composable. A buyer or agent can pay a few cents for one narrow task instead of adopting a large workflow platform. The product is useful when the cost of repetitive first-pass research is higher than the cost of an automated evidence primitive.
